title: Coding Agents
description: Learn to deploy and manage autonomous coding agents to execute complex, multi-file refactors and architectural changes.
learning_objectives: Distinguish between standard AI assistants and autonomous coding agents
Configure a coding agent environment using tools like Cursor or Claude Code
Execute a wide-scale refactor across multiple files using an agentic workflow
Verify and audit agent-generated changes through diff reviews and test suites
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with Git version control
Experience with AI chat interfaces (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude)

sections.heading: From Copilots to Agents
sections.content_brief: Explain the shift from autocomplete/chat (Copilots) to agents that can read files, run terminal commands, and edit code autonomously. Discuss the 'Agentic Loop': Perceive, Plan, Act, and Evaluate.

sections.heading: Setting Up Your Agentic Environment
sections.content_brief: Walk through the installation and initialization of a coding agent (e.g., Claude Code CLI or Cursor). Explain the importance of codebase indexing/embedding for providing the agent with global context.
sections.code_context: Installing and initializing a CLI-based coding agent

sections.heading: Executing Wide-Scale Refactors
sections.content_brief: Demonstrate how to prompt an agent for a multi-file change, such as updating a deprecated API signature or migrating a data model. Contrast 'single-file' prompting with 'project-wide' instructions.
sections.code_context: Example of a high-level agentic prompt for a multi-file refactor

sections.heading: The Human-in-the-Loop: Review and Verification
sections.content_brief: Detail the process of auditing agent changes. Cover reviewing diffs, running existing test suites to catch regressions, and providing iterative feedback to the agent to fix errors.
sections.code_context: Running tests and using git diff to verify agentic changes

admonitions.content: Always ensure you are on a clean Git branch before initiating an agentic refactor. Agents can modify dozens of files in seconds, making it impossible to undo changes manually without version control.
If an agent gets stuck in a loop or fails to fix a bug after two attempts, provide a specific hint about the file or logic it is missing rather than asking it to 'try again'.
